account:
It is seven in the evening, and I am home for my scheduled engagement. Today's unusual business has been a vague rumor about changes to the bridge or port. I have not seen any such change or received a concrete proposal. My neighbour mentioned the rumor at tea but said they had seen nothing unusual themselves; I still do not know their source. The secretary traced another mention to Townsfolk 03, who directed them to the innkeeper. The innkeeper denied proposing or announcing any change. I have asked the secretary to arrange a conversation with Townsfolk 03 tomorrow, without displacing my appointments.

The reports available to me suggest ordinary activity rather than an established emergency: the neighbour described quiet docks and ordinary bread trade, and relayed that the baker had no special celebration planned. The secretary's accounts record says the builder found the bridge passable with no confirmed defects and relayed Freight's report of undamaged roads and an uneventful morning ferry crossing. The builder has been asking residents about specific repair needs and offering written estimates. No actual repair need, claim, receipt, or authorized spending has been established.

I suspect there may be some talk circulating that I have not yet understood, but I cannot say that anyone is organizing something secretly or what its purpose would be. Bridge or port alterations are only the subject of the rumor, not a confirmed plan. Tomorrow I should hear Townsfolk 03 firsthand and read my appointment book, which the secretary has promised to keep ready.
